requirements.quote:
This section lists the defined QUIC transport error codes that can be
   used in a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with a type of 0x1c.  These errors
   apply to the entire connection.
requirements.condition: When a defined QUIC transport error code from this section is carried in a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame
requirements.required_behavior: Use a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame of type 0x1c, with the error applying to the entire connection.
requirements.why_checkable: The CONNECTION_CLOSE frame type and connection-wide scope can be checked in frame construction and connection state handling.

requirements.quote:
NO_ERROR (0x00):  An endpoint uses this with CONNECTION_CLOSE to
      signal that the connection is being closed abruptly in the absence
      of any error.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint abruptly closes a connection in the absence of an error
requirements.error_behavior: Signal an error-free abrupt connection closure with NO_ERROR (0x00).
requirements.why_checkable: A test can inspect the error code emitted for an error-free abrupt closure.

requirements.quote:
INTERNAL_ERROR (0x01):  The endpoint encountered an internal error
      and cannot continue with the connection.
requirements.condition: When the endpoint encounters an internal error and cannot continue the connection
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted transport error code can be checked after a fatal internal error.

requirements.quote:
CONNECTION_REFUSED (0x02):  The server refused to accept a new
      connection.
requirements.condition: When a server refuses to accept a new connection
requirements.why_checkable: A connection-refusal test can inspect the transport error code selected by the server.

requirements.quote:
FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR (0x03):  An endpoint received more data than it
      permitted in its advertised data limits; see Section 4.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives more data than permitted by its advertised data limits
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exceed an advertised data limit and verify the selected error code.

requirements.quote:
STREAM_LIMIT_ERROR (0x04):  An endpoint received a frame for a stream
      identifier that exceeded its advertised stream limit for the
      corresponding stream type.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a frame whose stream identifier exceeds the advertised limit for that stream type
requirements.why_checkable: The stream identifier, stream type, advertised limit, and resulting error code are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
STREAM_STATE_ERROR (0x05):  An endpoint received a frame for a stream
      that was not in a state that permitted that frame; see Section 3.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a frame that is not permitted in the stream's current state
requirements.why_checkable: A test can establish a stream state, inject a disallowed frame, and inspect the resulting error code.

requirements.quote:
FINAL_SIZE_ERROR (0x06):  (1) An endpoint received a STREAM frame
      containing data that exceeded the previously established final
      size, (2) an endpoint received a STREAM frame or a RESET_STREAM
      frame containing a final size that was lower than the size of
      stream data that was already received, or (3) an endpoint received
      a STREAM frame or a RESET_STREAM frame containing a different
      final size to the one already established.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a STREAM frame containing data beyond the previously established final size
requirements.why_checkable: A test can establish a final size, send STREAM data beyond it, and verify the error code.

requirements.quote:
FINAL_SIZE_ERROR (0x06):  (1) An endpoint received a STREAM frame
      containing data that exceeded the previously established final
      size, (2) an endpoint received a STREAM frame or a RESET_STREAM
      frame containing a final size that was lower than the size of
      stream data that was already received, or (3) an endpoint received
      a STREAM frame or a RESET_STREAM frame containing a different
      final size to the one already established.
requirements.condition: When a STREAM or RESET_STREAM frame declares a final size lower than the amount of stream data already received
requirements.why_checkable: The declared final size and previously received byte extent can be compared and the resulting code inspected.

requirements.quote:
FINAL_SIZE_ERROR (0x06):  (1) An endpoint received a STREAM frame
      containing data that exceeded the previously established final
      size, (2) an endpoint received a STREAM frame or a RESET_STREAM
      frame containing a final size that was lower than the size of
      stream data that was already received, or (3) an endpoint received
      a STREAM frame or a RESET_STREAM frame containing a different
      final size to the one already established.
requirements.condition: When a STREAM or RESET_STREAM frame declares a final size different from the final size already established
requirements.why_checkable: A test can establish one final size, declare another, and verify the resulting error code.

requirements.quote:
FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR (0x07):  An endpoint received a frame that was
      badly formatted -- for instance, a frame of an unknown type or an
      ACK frame that has more acknowledgment ranges than the remainder
      of the packet could carry.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a badly formatted frame
requirements.error_behavior: Classify the malformed frame as FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR (0x07).
requirements.why_checkable: Malformed frame inputs can be supplied and the resulting transport error code inspected.

requirements.quote:
FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR (0x07):  An endpoint received a frame that was
      badly formatted -- for instance, a frame of an unknown type or an
      ACK frame that has more acknowledgment ranges than the remainder
      of the packet could carry.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives a frame of an unknown type
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the frame as badly formatted and classify it as FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR (0x07).
requirements.why_checkable: The paragraph explicitly identifies an unknown frame type as an instance of malformed frame encoding.

requirements.quote:
FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR (0x07):  An endpoint received a frame that was
      badly formatted -- for instance, a frame of an unknown type or an
      ACK frame that has more acknowledgment ranges than the remainder
      of the packet could carry.
requirements.condition: When an ACK frame declares more acknowledgment ranges than can fit in the remainder of the packet
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the ACK frame as badly formatted and classify it as FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR (0x07).
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded range count and remaining packet bytes can be compared, and the selected error code verified.

requirements.quote:
TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR (0x08):  An endpoint received transport
      parameters that were badly formatted, included an invalid value,
      omitted a mandatory transport parameter, included a forbidden
      transport parameter, or were otherwise in error.
requirements.condition: When received transport parameters are badly formatted
requirements.why_checkable: Malformed transport-parameter encodings can be supplied and the error code inspected.

requirements.quote:
TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR (0x08):  An endpoint received transport
      parameters that were badly formatted, included an invalid value,
      omitted a mandatory transport parameter, included a forbidden
      transport parameter, or were otherwise in error.
requirements.condition: When received transport parameters include an invalid value
requirements.why_checkable: An invalid parameter value can be injected and the resulting code verified.

requirements.quote:
TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR (0x08):  An endpoint received transport
      parameters that were badly formatted, included an invalid value,
      omitted a mandatory transport parameter, included a forbidden
      transport parameter, or were otherwise in error.
requirements.condition: When received transport parameters omit a mandatory transport parameter
requirements.why_checkable: A mandatory parameter can be omitted in a test input and the resulting code verified.

requirements.quote:
TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR (0x08):  An endpoint received transport
      parameters that were badly formatted, included an invalid value,
      omitted a mandatory transport parameter, included a forbidden
      transport parameter, or were otherwise in error.
requirements.condition: When received transport parameters include a forbidden transport parameter
requirements.why_checkable: A forbidden parameter can be included in test input and the resulting code verified.

requirements.quote:
TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR (0x08):  An endpoint received transport
      parameters that were badly formatted, included an invalid value,
      omitted a mandatory transport parameter, included a forbidden
      transport parameter, or were otherwise in error.
requirements.condition: When received transport parameters are otherwise in error
requirements.why_checkable: The passage does not define what additional conditions constitute being otherwise in error.

requirements.quote:
CONNECTION_ID_LIMIT_ERROR (0x09):  The number of connection IDs
      provided by the peer exceeds the advertised
      active_connection_id_limit.
requirements.condition: When the peer provides more connection IDs than the advertised active_connection_id_limit
requirements.why_checkable: The received connection-ID count can be compared with the advertised numeric limit and the error code inspected.

requirements.quote:
PROTOCOL_VIOLATION (0x0a):  An endpoint detected an error with
      protocol compliance that was not covered by more specific error
      codes.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint detects a protocol-compliance error not covered by a more specific error code
requirements.why_checkable: For a known compliance violation lacking a specific code, a test can inspect whether the generic protocol-violation code is selected.

requirements.quote:
INVALID_TOKEN (0x0b):  A server received a client Initial that
      contained an invalid Token field.
requirements.condition: When a server receives a client Initial containing an invalid Token field
requirements.why_checkable: A client Initial with an invalid Token can be injected and the server's error code inspected.

requirements.quote:
APPLICATION_ERROR (0x0c):  The application or application protocol
      caused the connection to be closed.
requirements.condition: When the application or application protocol causes the connection to close
requirements.why_checkable: A test-triggered application closure can be correlated with the emitted transport error code.

requirements.quote:
CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED (0x0d):  An endpoint has received more data in
      CRYPTO frames than it can buffer.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint receives more CRYPTO-frame data than it can buffer
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exceed the implementation's CRYPTO buffering capacity and inspect the emitted code.

requirements.quote:
KEY_UPDATE_ERROR (0x0e):  An endpoint detected errors in performing
      key updates; see Section 6 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When an endpoint detects an error while performing key updates
requirements.why_checkable: A key-update failure can be induced and the resulting transport error code inspected.

requirements.quote:
AEAD_LIMIT_REACHED (0x0f):  An endpoint has reached the
      confidentiality or integrity limit for the AEAD algorithm used by
      the given connection.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint reaches the confidentiality or integrity limit of the connection's AEAD algorithm
requirements.why_checkable: AEAD usage counters can be driven to a configured limit and the selected error code verified.

requirements.quote:
NO_VIABLE_PATH (0x10):  An endpoint has determined that the network
      path is incapable of supporting QUIC.  An endpoint is unlikely to
      receive a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame carrying this code except when
      the path does not support a large enough MTU.
requirements.condition: When an endpoint determines that the network path cannot support QUIC
requirements.why_checkable: A path deemed nonviable by the implementation can be correlated with its selected transport error code.

requirements.quote:
CRYPTO_ERROR (0x0100-0x01ff):  The cryptographic handshake failed.  A
      range of 256 values is reserved for carrying error codes specific
      to the cryptographic handshake that is used.  Codes for errors
      occurring when TLS is used for the cryptographic handshake are
      described in Section 4.8 of [QUIC-TLS].
requirements.condition: When the cryptographic handshake fails and a handshake-specific error code is carried
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the error within the 256-value CRYPTO_ERROR range 0x0100 through 0x01ff.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use values outside 0x0100 through 0x01ff as CRYPTO_ERROR values.
requirements.error_behavior: Carry a code specific to the cryptographic handshake failure.
requirements.why_checkable: The numeric range contains exactly 256 values and can be validated directly against an encoded error code.
